claims.text: In a transverse section of a herbaceous dicotyledonous stem, the epidermis is the outer layer, beneath it lies the cortex, and the vascular bundles form a ring around a central pith; in each bundle the xylem lies towards the pith and the phloem towards the outside, with a thin band of dividing cells (cambium) between them.

claims.text: A mature xylem vessel element is a long, hollow cell with no living contents, whose side walls are thickened with lignin in rings, spirals or a network leaving thin areas called pits; the end walls are broken down or perforated, so that vessel elements joined end to end form a continuous tube.

verification.method: Authored under standard v0.2.0-draft from the syllabus wording and our own knowledge of standard biology. Single source: no second source checked. Requires semantic review and two-source verification before any publication.

notes: verification_state: single_source. Syllabus wording names 'xylem vessel elements'. Xylem also contains fibres and parenchyma, which the syllabus does not name and which are left out. The mature vessel element is dead; lignin is in the wall, not in the lumen.

claims.text: A sieve tube element is a living cell with a cellulose wall, a thin lining of cytoplasm, few organelles and no nucleus when mature; sieve tube elements are joined end to end, and their end walls are perforated by pores to form sieve plates, so that the cytoplasm of neighbouring elements is continuous.

verification.method: Authored under standard v0.2.0-draft from the syllabus wording and our own knowledge of standard biology. Single source: no second source checked. Requires semantic review and two-source verification before any publication.

notes: verification_state: single_source. Standard description. The cytoplasm is a thin layer pressed against the wall, leaving a wide central lumen for sap.

claims.text: A companion cell lies beside each sieve tube element and has a nucleus, dense cytoplasm and many mitochondria; it is joined to its sieve tube element by plasmodesmata, which are narrow channels of cytoplasm through the cell wall.

verification.method: Authored under standard v0.2.0-draft from the syllabus wording and our own knowledge of standard biology. Single source: no second source checked. Requires semantic review and two-source verification before any publication.

notes: verification_state: single_source. Standard description. Plasmodesmata are too fine to be resolved with a light microscope, so on a slide a companion cell is recognised by its size, position and dense cytoplasm.

claims.text: The lignin in the walls of xylem vessel elements strengthens them so that they resist collapsing inwards when water is pulled up under tension, and makes the walls waterproof; the empty lumen and the lack of end walls give little resistance to the flow of water up the plant, and pits let water pass sideways between neighbouring vessels and to living cells.

notes: verification_state: single_source. Condition kept in the text: collapse is resisted when water in the vessel is under tension (pulled up from above). The mechanism of the pull belongs to the transpiration topic and is not taught here.

claims.text: Sieve tubes carry sucrose and amino acids in solution (phloem sap) from where they are made or released to where they are used or stored; the pores in the sieve plates and the wide, largely empty lumen let sap flow through, and the companion cells supply the ATP that the loading of sucrose into the sieve tube needs.

notes: verification_state: single_source. The direction of flow (from source to sink) and the loading process belong to the translocation topic; here only the structural links are given. claims.text: Xylem vessels are made of cells, not of lignin: lignin is a substance in the walls of the vessel elements, and the cells have died, leaving an empty lumen with no cytoplasm or organelles, which is why the resistance to the flow of water is low; saying only that the xylem has more space is not an explanation.

notes: verification_state: single_source. Standard biology. claims.text: On a prepared slide in longitudinal section, a xylem vessel appears as a long tube with an empty lumen and thick walls marked by rings, spirals or pits, while a sieve tube appears as a column of thin-walled cells with cross walls (sieve plates) and a narrower companion cell with a nucleus and dense cytoplasm beside it; in transverse section the vessels have wide, empty, thick-walled outlines and the sieve tube elements are wide and thin-walled beside smaller companion cells.
